paragraphs.text: These are Yunnan tea buds picked in early spring while still tightly closed, foraged from wild trees rather than gathered from a tended garden. They were dried just as they came off the branch, with no heat applied to stop their change and no rolling.

That places them in [white tea](white:definition), the style made with the fewest steps: the leaf is only withered and dried. Because it is never heated, rolled or bruised, each bud keeps its natural shape and the white down that gives the style its name. In [Yunnan white](yunnan-white:making) the leaf is finished by air rather than given the low final bake that Fujian white tea usually receives.

brewing.text: Yunnan white is brewed gently, as a white tea is, in a gaiwan or small pot, and it gives many infusions; the leaf holds up well.

notice.text: A honeyed, sweet cup, often richer and fuller than Fujian white, with little bitterness, sometimes fruit like apricot or melon and a hay or herbal note. Yabao is sweet and silky, often with pine or herbal notes.
